- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.23) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–8% from forecast for next 7–10 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.16 for 3+ consecutive days), model underestimates; add 1–4% to forecast for next 5–7 days.  
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 1.5–2x recent 7-day average for first 5 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >+10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.23 to -0.16) triggers “reversion” rule: forecast should drop 2–5% for next 3–5 days unless confirmed by new data.
